content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I developed a [product_name] project using [product_name] software and a [product_name] website editor. When I connect my [product_name] device directly to my PC via Ethernet and access the web page, everything works correctly. However, if I connect the [product_name] to my home router and access the website from my laptop or smartphone using WiFi (or mobile internet with port forwarding), the site loads but none of the interactive elements—like toggle buttons or number input fields—respond. The time counters also don't work. Has anyone experienced this issue before? Any suggested solutions?
Are you trying to connect to the [product_name] device through the internet rather than just your home network?
My intention is to access the device from outside my local network, but I encounter the same issue even when my PC or smartphone is connected to my home network.

Is the device's IP address assigned by your home router's DHCP? Have you tried connecting your laptop to the home network with Ethernet while turning off WiFi? Are ports 80 and 443 restricted or redirected for any of these devices?

You can connect through a router, but the device must be on the same network. Static IP and port forwarding alone often don't work. I resolved a similar issue by implementing my own VPN: both routers maintain a constant connection, and you access the site via a VPN with shared rules. (Brands like Mikrotik or Teltonika work well for this purpose.) If you don't want to learn how to set this up, consider hiring a professional to save time. As a warning: I manage a remote site that controls water levels, where the client previously used an older web server accessed through VPN over a cellular connection. When we upgraded to a custom web page for improved usability, things worked perfectly during bench testing and at installation. However, later the websites would sometimes get stuck on "Loading." Fortunately, I provided an alternative "old school" access path to ensure reliability. For sites far away, the website editor sometimes refuses to communicate with the device even through VPN. I might make a new thread for that. I recommend having a headless PC running Windows and [company_name] utilities at the remote site, so you can access it reliably via remote desktop tools like TeamViewer or AnyDesk.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience serious responsiveness problems with websites generated by [product_name] editing tools when accessed through a home router, both locally and remotely with port forwarding. Although the page loads, interactive controls fail to function, preventing effective local and remote control, which is essential for their project.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that websites created with [product_name] editing software will function reliably and remain responsive over both local and remote networks using a home router.
